analysis: What changed versus the 8:00 AM brief: the tape bounced off its lows instead of breaking further — but only slightly. At about 10:57 AM ET the S&P was -3.37% and the Nasdaq-100 -5.65%; by about 11:31 AM ET SPY had recovered to -2.90% (low 737.14) and QQQ to -4.60% (low 647.50), and the latest StockSetups read (11:54 AM ET) has SPY -3.14% and QQQ -4.79% — so the morning is ending in a choppy, partial rebound, not a fresh leg down. The day's landmark is now set: the Nasdaq Composite fell more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record close (27,599.89), putting it on track to confirm a correction, and the dpa-AFX midday wire has the Nasdaq at its lowest intraday level in over six months. Megacaps are all red but the dispersion narrowed: Apple (-1.23%) is the relative haven, Alphabet (-1.86%) and Amazon (-1.78%) are holding up better than the tape, while Meta (-3.69%), Microsoft (-2.40%) and Nvidia (-6.90%) keep sliding. Tesla (-9.05%) and SpaceX (-8.40%) are the day's political unwind, with the merger-by-year-end probability down to 9.5% and ARK buying $47.4M of SpaceX into the fall. The Bank of England's first hike since 2023 (8-1, to 4%, with a hawkish dissent wanting 4.25%) adds a global tightening wrinkle, and the WSB thread flags two new policy items: Rep. Ansari calling for a pause in advanced AI development and a Trump-administration licensing dispute over SK Hynix's Dalian plant — both single-source via that analysis, unconfirmed elsewhere. Signal vs noise: the correction confirmation, the memory-complex capitulation (MU low $656, SNDK low $807) and the broadening policy overhang are signal; the intraday V-bounce chatter, unverified fund-blowup rumors (Walleye/Engineers Gate) and the 'hotline marked the bottom' meme are noise. The rebound is concentrated in the hardest-hit names (SOXL +17% off its low, MU/SNDK ~8% off lows) on lighter volume — covering, not breadth improving.

community_signals.takeaway: Updated 11:06-11:30 ET window (1,500 comments): fear/greed ~20/100, up from ~10 at the lows. The thread is split between a 'V-shaped rebound of the century' camp and a 'fake V / bull trap' camp; SPY recovered only ~1% from its low (737) with 745 seen as resistance. New items beyond the headlines: Rep. Ansari calling for a pause in advanced AI development, a Trump-administration licensing dispute over SK Hynix's Dalian plant, and unverified rumors that Walleye and Engineers Gate closed equity pods. The analysis also corrects a viral misread: SOXX's apparent ~70% plunge was a display artifact of its 3-for-1 split (split-adjusted about -8.7%).

headlines.headline: The Nasdaq Composite fell more than 10% below its Oct. 6 record close of 27,599.89, putting it on track to confirm a correction if it closes there, Reuters reported. As of about 11:05 AM ET the Nasdaq was -5.32% at 24,366.28; the S&P 500 was -3.50% at 7,419.52 and the Dow -2.32% at 52,117.55. The latest StockSetups read (11:54 AM ET, 15-min delayed) has SPY $742.63 (-3.14%), QQQ $658.75 (-4.79%) and DIA $520.31 (-2.39%) — off the morning lows (SPY low 737.14, QQQ low 647.50).
headlines.why_it_matters: Correction territory is a line the tape now has to reckon with — and the bounce off the lows is partial, so the session is stabilizing rather than reversing.

headlines.headline: Nvidia fell 6.90% to $186.32 (low $181.55, prior close $200.13) in late-morning trading. The Reuters report from this morning still stands: about 600,000 H200 chips are stored in Hong Kong awaiting Beijing import approval. Nvidia reports fiscal Q3 on Tuesday, Nov 17, having guided revenue to about $108 billion.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI leader is now down about 7% on the day and roughly 13.5% over five sessions — the tape is de-risking ahead of the Nov 17 print, not waiting for it.

headlines.headline: The memory rout kept grinding: AMD fell 12.80% to $426.30, Micron fell 11.59% to $702.38 (intraday low $656.12), SanDisk fell 16.61% to $864.79 (low $807.30), Qualcomm fell 11.44% to $153.86 and the 3x-long SOXL fell 28.85%. The iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) slid about 9% and the PHLX Semiconductor Index was down about 11% in the latest Yahoo Finance-cited figures.
headlines.why_it_matters: Memory is still the epicenter and the declines are deepening into their third session — a beat (AMD) and a halted plant (Micron) are both being sold, which says the complex is being repriced, not traded on news.

headlines.headline: Tesla fell 9.05% to about $350.34 and SpaceX fell 8.40% to $124.50 in late-morning trading. Musk's net worth fell about $33.5 billion on Wednesday to $865 billion; Cathie Wood's ARK bought $47.4 million of SpaceX on Wednesday, and the probability of a Tesla-SpaceX merger announcement by Dec 31 has fallen to 9.5%.
headlines.why_it_matters: The political unwind is accelerating — Tesla is now down roughly 12% across the two sessions since the election, and the merger-premium story is losing its cushion while a buyer steps in on the other side.

headlines.headline: The megacap split has narrowed but all seven are red: Apple $345.20 (-1.23%), Alphabet $283.57 (-1.86%), Amazon $261.30 (-1.78%), Microsoft $542.49 (-2.40%), Meta $606.76 (-3.69%), Nvidia $186.32 (-6.90%) and Tesla ~$350.34 (-9.05%). Apple remains the relative haven; Meta has now given back most of its post-earnings cushion.
headlines.why_it_matters: The selloff is broad across megacaps now, but the dispersion matters — Apple, Alphabet and Amazon holding near -1% to -2% is what keeps the index loss near -3% instead of -5%.

headlines.headline: The Bank of England raised rates for the first time in over three years, hiking Bank Rate 8-1 to 4% from 3.75%, and warned at least one more increase was likely if the US-Iran conflict continues. The dissent came from Catherine Mann, who wanted a bigger half-point hike to 4.25%. UK inflation is seen reaching around 5% by mid-2027.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hawkish hike from a major central bank on a day the tape is already fragile — global tightening pressure is a headwind for growth multiples, even if the direct US impact is limited.

headlines.headline: AppLovin is still up about 28.5-28.9% at roughly $350 after Q3 revenue jumped 55% to $2.18 billion (vs $2.07 billion expected), EPS of $4.30 beat the $4.03 consensus, and it guided Q4 revenue to $2.365-2.395 billion (vs $2.25 billion expected) plus a $3.2 billion buyback add.
headlines.why_it_matters: The morning's clearest earnings counterweight is still holding nearly all of its gain — a genuine blowout with a raised guide — but it is one name against a broad tape.

headlines.headline: Initial jobless claims fell to 189,000 last week, the fewest since mid-July, the Labor Department reported at 8:30 AM ET — a strong labor print heading into Friday's payrolls. It is still being ignored by a tape dominated by chips and AI-policy headlines.
headlines.why_it_matters: A genuinely strong labor print that would normally support the tape, but it is being ignored while chips dominate the session — a sign the move is sentiment- and positioning-driven, not macro-driven.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC news this morning; the Nov 3 Q3 story carries forward: record revenue $357.2M (+43% year over year, vs ~$348.32M consensus), record Adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF coverage 1.67x, EPS $0.33 vs $0.3345 expected, distribution held at $0.525, full-year guidance tightened to Adjusted EBITDA $770-780M and DCF $495-505M. The $0.525 distribution pays tomorrow, Friday Nov 6. On the earnings call, management said over 60% of 2027 horsepower deliveries are contracted (about 90% of first-half deliveries), but flagged cost pressure: monthly lubricant costs exited Q3 about 25% above first-half levels and diesel hit an all-time high in September, with pricing not yet fully reflecting the increases.

watch_next: Friday Nov 6, 8:30 a.m. ET: October nonfarm payrolls (about 59,000-62,000 jobs expected, up from 29,000 in September; unemployment expected to hold at 4.2%); USAC's $0.525 distribution pays.
After the close today: Airbnb (EPS est. $2.85, revenue est. $4.75B), Cloudflare, Monster Beverage, Microchip Technology and IREN report Q3 results.
Whether the late-morning bounce holds into the close or fades — SPY's intraday low was 737.14 with 745 seen as overhead resistance; a break below 737 reopens the morning's lows.
